questions.scenario: The nurse is comparing several renal function trends for a client whose kidney status is worsening.

options.text: Supports worsening acute kidney injury
Less urgent monitoring picture

matrixRows.label: Rising creatinine with falling urine output
Stable creatinine with adequate hourly urine output
Improved intake with steady daily weight

questions.rationale: Acute kidney injury becomes more urgent when urine output falls, creatinine rises, and electrolyte complications emerge. Stable output and renal trends belong on the less urgent side because they do not signal deterioration.

questions.stem: Which finding in this newly transplanted client should the nurse treat as the strongest evidence of acute kidney rejection?
questions.scenario: A client is 14 days after kidney transplant and reports malaise, tenderness over the graft, and lower urine output than yesterday.
questions.additionalInfo: Morning data: temperature 100.8 F (38.2 C), creatinine up from 1.1 to 1.9 mg/dL, blood pressure 148/92 mm Hg, incision clean and dry.

options.text: Rising creatinine with graft tenderness and falling urine output
Mild hand tremor after the tacrolimus dose
Poor appetite and mild constipation
Trace edema at the ankles after walking

questions.rationale: Acute rejection is recognized fastest by clustering graft tenderness, reduced urine output, and worsening kidney function. The nurse should move toward urgent escalation instead of anchoring on medication side effects or vague discomfort.

distractorRationales.b: "Mild hand tremor after the tacrolimus dose" misses the bedside risk. The cue "2 C), creatinine up from 1" points to medication toxicity. Medication safety depends on checking contraindications, labs, and adverse effects before giving or continuing the drug.
distractorRationales.c: The cue "lower urine output than yesterday" suggests medication toxicity, so "Poor appetite and mild constipation" would not correct the active problem. Medication safety depends on checking contraindications, labs, and adverse effects before giving or continuing the drug.
distractorRationales.d: The option can leave medication toxicity untreated because it moves to activity, intake, or discharge planning too early. "Rising creatinine with graft tenderness and falling urine output" fits the safer response to the cue "9 mg/dL, blood pressure 148/92 mm Hg, incision clean and dry".

questions.takeaway: In a fresh transplant, graft tenderness plus kidney decline is rejection until proven otherwise.
questions.speedCue: Time from transplant plus graft pain plus creatinine rise is the clue cluster that should outrank softer postoperative complaints.
